question.text: Which of the following must be submitted to SEBI by a PM on quarterly basis?

explanation.text: The Logic: Among the options listed, the only items that a portfolio manager is expected to report to SEBI in a periodic regulatory filing are operational metrics such as AUM and performance. Client birthdays, internal management memos and ordinary advertising content are not part of any periodic SEBI submission for a PM. The Trap: Client birthdays are personal-relationship data and have no regulatory relevance; internal memos are confidential management documents, not regulatory submissions; advertising content is governed by separate marketing-material rules, not by a periodic AUM/performance return. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook pages checked (pp. 129, 154, 361, 385) refer to periodic reports / disclosure-document declarations, SEBI's right to call for portfolio particulars / client names / net worth as required (p. 154), the rule that marketing performance must match what is reported to SEBI (p. 361) and client reports furnished at intervals not exceeding three months (p. 385), but do not state a quarterly SEBI submission of AUM / performance / NAV / client numbers in those exact terms. The framing above reflects general PM regulatory practice rather than a workbook citation.
